stories.headline: Denver Police Reopen 13 Sexual Assault Cases Tied to Disgraced CBI DNA Analyst
stories.summary:
The Denver Police Department has reopened and is retesting evidence in 13 sexual assault cases linked to former Colorado Bureau of Investigation DNA analyst Yvonne "Missy" Woods, who was sentenced to prison this week for manipulating and mishandling forensic evidence. The retesting effort aims to determine whether Woods' misconduct affected the outcomes of those cases.

Woods' crimes have cast a shadow over the CBI's forensic laboratory and raised concerns about the integrity of convictions and investigations that relied on her DNA analysis. The scope of her misconduct has prompted scrutiny of the agency's oversight procedures.

Denver investigators say the retesting process is ongoing. Authorities have not specified how long the review is expected to take or whether any charges or convictions may be revisited as a result.

stories.headline: 18-Year-Old Arrested in Fatal Brighton Shooting
stories.summary:
Brighton police arrested Jeness Torres, 18, early Sunday morning on suspicion of second-degree murder after a shooting in the 3100 block of Eagle Boulevard left a 33-year-old man dead. Officers responded to the scene around 12:30 a.m. and found the victim, who was transported to a hospital where he later died from his injuries.

The victim's identity is pending release by the Adams County Coroner's Office. Police have not disclosed a motive or the circumstances that led to the shooting.

Anyone with information is asked to contact the Brighton Police Department tip line at 303-655-8740, referencing case 12CN26005049. The investigation is ongoing.

stories.headline: Three Shot in Colorado Springs Early Sunday; Suspect Still at Large
stories.summary:
Colorado Springs Police are searching for an unidentified suspect after three people were shot around 2:20 a.m. Sunday on South Circle Drive south of Airport Road. Officers found one woman shot at the scene and provided aid until medical personnel arrived; two additional victims — a man and a woman — drove themselves to the hospital.

All three victims sustained gunshot wounds and were reported in serious but stable condition. No suspects had been identified as of Sunday morning, and detectives from the Colorado Springs Police Assault Unit are leading the investigation.

Authorities have not released information about a possible motive or what led to the shooting.

stories.headline: Boy Shot at Longmont Dollar Tree; Suspect Sought
stories.summary:
Longmont police are investigating a shooting at a Dollar Tree on the 2200 block of Main Street that injured a juvenile male Sunday afternoon. Officers responded around 2:45 p.m. after an altercation between a man and a boy under 18 escalated outside the store.

Investigators say the boy picked up a weapon during the confrontation, at which point the suspect drew a firearm and fired multiple rounds, striking the juvenile at least once. The boy was transported to an area hospital for treatment.

Authorities are still searching for the suspect. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Longmont Police Department at 303-774-3700.

stories.headline: Democratic Candidate's First Attack Ads Against Rep. Jeff Crank Contain Misleading Claims, Colorado Sun Finds
stories.summary:
Democrat Jessica Killin, who is seeking to flip Colorado's Republican-held 5th Congressional District, launched her first attack ads against incumbent U.S. Rep. Jeff Crank, but the Colorado Sun found both spots contain misleading characterizations. The ads claim Crank requested a special waiver to accept gifts from lobbyists behind closed doors without disclosure — a description that omits significant context.

Crank applied for a standard gift-disclosure waiver from the House Ethics Committee in March 2025 in connection with his daughter's wedding, a routine and bipartisan process that requires sign-off from both the Republican and Democratic leaders of the committee. Both leaders approved the waiver, and Crank's office says no lobbyists were invited to the wedding and no gifts were ultimately received.

The ads crop or blur the bipartisan signatures on the waiver document, obscuring that the exemption was approved by members of both parties. Crank's campaign called the ads a "desperate attempt" to smear him. Killin would be the first Democrat to represent the district, which includes Colorado Springs.

stories.headline: Denver Launches Online System to Dispute Parking Tickets After Previous Platform Was Cut
stories.summary:
The City and County of Denver has introduced a new online portal allowing residents to contest parking tickets, restoring a digital dispute option that was shut down last year due to budget cuts. The new system is intended to give drivers a more convenient alternative to disputing citations in person.

The city did not immediately detail how the new platform differs from its predecessor or what technical or financial safeguards have been put in place to ensure continuity. The restoration of the service comes as Denver officials have been working to modernize and streamline city services.

stories.headline: More Than 350 Flights Delayed at Denver International Airport After Ground Stop
stories.summary:
More than 350 flights at Denver International Airport were delayed Sunday afternoon after the Federal Aviation Administration issued an hour-long ground stop citing high airport volume. The ground stop, which affected arriving flights, began shortly before 4:30 p.m. and was lifted around 5:30 p.m.

As of 5:45 p.m., FlightAware data showed 356 delayed flights and two cancellations. Southwest Airlines accounted for the largest share of delays with 167 affected flights, followed by United with 87, SkyWest with 37, Delta with 19, American Airlines with 14, and Frontier with 13.

Southwest and Frontier each canceled one flight. The disruptions affected travelers on one of the busiest travel days of the weekend. DIA is one of the nation's busiest airports, and volume-driven ground stops are not uncommon during peak travel periods.

stories.headline: Federal Agents Begin Large-Scale Helicopter Roundup of Wild Horses in Western Colorado
stories.summary:
The Bureau of Land Management has conducted its largest wild horse helicopter roundups in Colorado in several years, removing 880 horses from the Piceance-East Douglas Herd Management Area west of Meeker since early August. This week, the agency plans to begin a separate roundup targeting 245 horses in the Sand Wash Basin area west of Craig, where extreme summer drought has strained food and water resources.

The operations have drawn sharp criticism from Gov. Jared Polis and four of Colorado's congressional representatives, who sent a letter urging federal officials to halt the roundups and calling helicopter methods "inhumane and unnecessary." Nine horses died during the Piceance-East Douglas operation, which ran from Aug. 2 to Sept. 2; six were euthanized for preexisting conditions.

Wild horse management has long been contentious across the West. More than 60,000 horses are currently held in long-term federal holding facilities at a cost exceeding $100 million annually, consuming two-thirds of the BLM's wild horse program budget. The BLM says the horse populations in both Colorado management areas far exceed what the land can sustainably support.

stories.headline: Climber Rescued from North Table Mountain Near Golden After Equipment Failure
stories.summary:
A climber was rescued from North Table Mountain north of Golden last week after an equipment malfunction left them unable to move up or down the rock face, Arvada Fire officials said. Crews from both Arvada and Golden responded and established a new rope system to safely lower the climber to the ground.

No injuries were reported. Arvada Fire did not specify the exact date of the rescue or the type of equipment that failed.

"Rescues like this one, with a safe outcome for all involved, highlight why we train so thoroughly for any and all hazards," Arvada officials said in a statement. North Table Mountain is a popular destination for hikers and climbers in the Denver metro foothills.

stories.headline: Broncos' Bo Nix Set to Face Chiefs' Patrick Mahomes in Monday Night Opener at Arrowhead
stories.summary:
The Denver Broncos open the 2026 NFL season Monday night against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium in what is being framed as a marquee matchup between Bo Nix and Patrick Mahomes, both returning from offseason surgeries. Nix recovered from multiple procedures on his right ankle, while Mahomes underwent a more serious ACL repair on his left knee.

Denver Post columnist Troy Renck argues Nix is positioned to end Mahomes' seven-game home winning streak against the Broncos and establish Denver as the AFC West's dominant team. The Broncos enter the season as the reigning AFC's top playoff seed, having won 25 games in Nix's first two seasons.

New offensive coordinator Davis Webb is expected to simplify play calls and give Nix more time to read defenses at the line of scrimmage. The team has also named nine captains for the 2026 season, with Nix drawing notice for a passionate address to teammates during the announcement. Kickoff is scheduled for 8:15 p.m.

stories.headline: Broncos Defense Prepares for Travis Kelce Challenge in Week 1
stories.summary:
The Denver Broncos face an immediate test of their pass defense Monday night when they meet Travis Kelce and the Kansas City Chiefs in the season opener. Kelce has accumulated 1,663 receiving yards against Denver over his career — the most against any single opponent — and tight ends as a position group gained 1,015 yards against Denver last season, ninth-most in the NFL.

Coach Sean Payton said Kelce's football intelligence and long-standing chemistry with Mahomes makes the veteran tight end uniquely difficult to defend, noting that extended plays are particularly dangerous against the pair. The Broncos plan to rotate multiple defenders on Kelce, including cornerback Jahdae Barron, nickelback Ja'Quan McMillian, linebackers Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad, and safety Talanoa Hufanga.

Barron, entering his second season, showed promise against Kelce in last year's Week 11 matchup, holding him to two catches for 14 yards on six man-coverage snaps and recording a pass breakup. At 36 years old and in his 14th season, Kelce remains Mahomes' primary target despite questions about his decline.

stories.headline: Nuggets Sign Bryce Hopkins to Two-Way Contract
stories.summary:
The Denver Nuggets have signed forward Bryce Hopkins to a two-way contract, the team announced. Two-way contracts allow players to split time between an NBA roster and the G League affiliate while counting against a separate roster limit from standard NBA contracts.

The signing adds depth to Denver's frontcourt as the team heads into the 2026-27 season. Hopkins' addition comes as the Nuggets continue to finalize their roster following the offseason signing of DeMar DeRozan, which was reported previously.

Details of the contract's financial terms were not disclosed. The Nuggets open their regular season later this fall.

topStory.headline: Wisconsin GOP Gubernatorial Candidate Tom Tiffany Survives Emergency Water Landing After Plane Loses Power
topStory.summary:
U.S. Rep. Tom Tiffany, the Republican candidate for Wisconsin governor, and pilot Leonard Boltz, 73, of Pearson, escaped with minor injuries Saturday night after their small aircraft lost power on approach to Wausau Downtown Airport and was forced to make an emergency water landing in Lake Wausau. Marathon County Emergency Dispatch received the initial 911 call at approximately 8:49 p.m. on Sept. 13. The aircraft, a four-seat Beechcraft K35 Bonanza, submerged after landing, and both occupants exited the plane and swam to a shallow area to await rescue.

Tiffany, recounting the incident at a Sunday news conference, said the pilot, identified by the Marathon County Sheriff's Office as Leonard Boltz, warned him with approximately 10 seconds to spare before impact, instructing him to tighten his seat belt. Tiffany said there was "no panic" as the two swam to a nearby sandbar. Both were located by Wausau Fire Department crews who deployed an airboat and a Rapid Deployment Craft, brought aboard the airboat, treated on shore by paramedics, and transported by ambulance to Aspirus Wausau Hospital, where they were treated and released. Tiffany required stitches above his right eye.

The multi-agency response included the Wausau Police Department, Marathon County Sheriff's Office, Wisconsin State Patrol, Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources, and the SAFER Fire Department. The aircraft remains submerged in Lake Wausau, and authorities have placed a no-wake buoy near the site, urging boaters to avoid the area until recovery crews can remove the wreckage. Both the Federal Aviation Administration and the National Transportation Safety Board have opened investigations into the incident.

Tiffany, who represents Wisconsin's 7th Congressional District and holds an endorsement from President Donald Trump in the Nov. 3 gubernatorial election, said the experience would not deter his campaign for governor. His Democratic opponent, Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley, extended well-wishes in a post on X, writing that he was "grateful to God that Congressman Tiffany and no one else was hurt in this horrifying incident, which could have been a tragedy if not for the heroism of the pilot."
